The loader now runs do-after-load-evaluation as GNU does, so loading a lisp/obsolete file runs GNU's obsolete-file warning, which autoloads bytecomp.el; bytecomp's eval-when-compile requires compile.el and simple.el, beyond the warm chain (which now reaches abbrev.el). These 16 files counted as loading only while Romacs skipped the hook. Owner-approved 2026-10-28; independent review: GPT Sol r1/r2 of the measurement change.

lisp/mail/mspools.el was recorded at 84daf78 from a shell with MAIL set; in a clean environment its defcustom reads rmail-spool-directory, whose custom-initialize-delay leaves it unbound until startup, past the warm chain. Re-measured with a minimal environment and the gate slot unlimited stack.
